title: U.S. Intelligence Warns of 'Advanced' Iranian Plots Targeting Americans Abroad
snippet: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned that Iranian plots to target U.S. personnel have reached advanced stages, prompting diplomatic evacuations and military adjustments across the Middle East.
content:
WASHINGTON — Top U.S. intelligence officials have issued a stark warning regarding heightened threats from Tehran, cautioning that Iranian plots to target and kill American personnel abroad have escalated to "advanced stages."

According to an unclassified memorandum sent to Secretary of State Marco Rubio by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, Tehran has substantially increased its efforts against U.S. citizens and government operatives, particularly in the Middle East and selected international locations. CIA Director John Ratcliffe was also briefed on the memo.

Diplomatic Drawdowns and Security Precautions

The intelligence warning comes as the State Department actively reevaluates security protocols and scales back diplomatic footprints throughout the region. Non-essential personnel and their families were recently ordered to evacuate the U.S. Embassy in Saudi Arabia, while multiple other missions have transitioned to "Restricted Operations" to minimize exposure without issuing formal evacuation orders.

Simultaneously, the Pentagon has begun quietly drawing down its military footprint at various outposts across the region due to the heightened risk environment.

Officials note that the elevated posture is driven not only by direct threats from Iranian operatives, but also by escalating attacks from the Iranian-backed Houthi movement in Yemen. Houthi militants have recently intensified drone and missile strikes against Saudi Arabian infrastructure, including a deadly strike at Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport that claimed the life of a U.S. citizen.

White House Considers Response

While Clayton’s memo did not name specific targets or confirm an imminent attack timeframe, intelligence agencies are currently working to downgrade sensitive intelligence so that detailed threat assessments can be shared more broadly among State Department personnel.

The threat warning arrives at a tense moment for U.S.-Iran relations, with the administration actively weighing whether to resume military strikes against Iranian assets. Addressing supporters at a campaign rally in Florida, President Trump indicated that further military operations remain a possibility if diplomatic negotiations fail to yield results.
